19	Part 1 - Problem Analysis (Kepner-Tregoe).
20	1. State the deviation precisely: what should be happening, what is actually happening, and the gap, in measurable terms. A complaint or opinion is not a deviation until it is specified.
21	2. Specify the problem along four dimensions, each as IS versus IS NOT:
22	   - WHAT: which object, unit, product or group shows the deviation, and which comparable ones that could but do not?
23	   - WHERE: in which locations, processes, teams or channels is it observed, and where is it not?
24	   - WHEN: when was it first observed, when since, under what conditions or cycle, and when not?
25	   - EXTENT: how many, how much, what trend, what share - and what is not affected?
26	3. For each IS/IS NOT pair, list distinctions: what is true of the IS that is not true of the IS NOT.
27	4. For each distinction, list changes: what changed in, on, around or about that distinction, and when.

40	8. Identify the indicators or evidence that would change the conclusion, and prefer collecting evidence that discriminates between the leading hypotheses.

44	2. Separate MUST objectives (mandatory, measurable, realistic) from WANT objectives (weighted by importance).
45	3. Screen alternatives against MUSTs; score surviving alternatives against WANTs.

55	CASE OD2-DEV2-CONTRA: Night premium shortfalls after the Fenmarch Water payroll cutover
56	
57	Setting: Fenmarch Water is a regional water utility with 2,140 staff. In October 2026 it moved payroll from an in-house legacy system to PayLattice, a hosted payroll platform supplied and configured by Ardentra Ltd. Two parallel-run cycles (August and September) were signed off on 9 October, and a configuration freeze started that day. The board had brought go-live forward by one pay period. The first live payroll was calculated on 27 October and paid on 30 October. Within days, night-shift staff began reporting underpayments. The November calculation is due on 24 November.
58	
59	Presenting request: From Anika Rautio, Chief Operating Officer, 17 Nov: 'Ardentra says our data caused the October pay errors, and Malcolm wants to act on that before the November calculation on 24 Nov. Before I sign anything off, tell me what actually caused the errors, whether Ardentra's account holds up, and which of the proposed actions we should take.'
60	
61	INITIAL EVIDENCE
62	E1 [stage S1] Ardentra incident report AR-INC-2291, G. Vos (Ardentra implementation lead), 10 Nov (vendor-account): Summary: the October underpayments come from source data quality. Our post-incident data audit found 212 employee records with malformed shift-pattern codes (trailing spaces, legacy 'N/S' prefixes). In PayLattice, premium eligibility is driven by shift-pattern code. The production load on 24 Oct used a fresh legacy extract (MD-1023) taken on 23 Oct, which carried these anomalies into production. 18 of the 139 complainants hold flagged records. The rest may carry anomalies that our audit rules do not detect. No change affecting pay calculation was made after parallel-run sign-off (see change log: CR-118 was a label correction). Recommendation: Fenmarch to re-cleanse and reload employee master data before the November run. Under clause 14.3, fixing client-data defects is at Fenmarch's cost.
63	E2 [stage S1] Ardentra-maintained change log extract, 9–28 Oct, supplied with AR-INC-2291 (change-record): CR-114 | 13 Oct | Bank file header field order corrected | calc impact: none | approved O. Calloway (Payroll Manager).
64	CR-118 | 22 Oct | NSP-02 (night shift premium): display label text correction 'Night Prem' → 'Night Shift Premium' | calc impact: none | test: not required | approved O. Calloway (CAB 21 Oct).
65	REL-7.4 | 24 Oct | PayLattice platform release 7.4, includes the statutory tax table update required from the November pay period | calc impact: platform | vendor regression pack passed.
66	CR-121 | 25 Oct | Payslip header logo replaced | calc impact: none.
67	Note: Ardentra consultants write the entries in this log when a change is requested.
68	E3 [stage S1] Payroll helpdesk ticket summary, generated 12 Nov; finance bank reconciliation note, 31 Oct (system-record): October pay tickets: 139, from 139 individuals. Every ticket reports an underpayment, and none reports an overpayment. All 139 cite the night shift premium line. No tickets concern basic pay, overtime, tax or deductions. Shortfalls claimed: £37–£201 per person, median £98. By directorate: Operations (treatment works shift teams) 124; Customer Contact overnight team 15. No tickets from staff who work days only. Finance bank reconciliation for the 30 Oct payment: the amounts credited matched the payroll output file for all 2,140 payees.
69	E4 [stage S1] Email, Malcolm Treharne (Programme Director) to COO, 11 Nov (leadership-account): Ardentra's report makes it clear this is our data. I signed off the cleanse on the strength of the vendor's assurance, and I won't let the November run go wrong for the same reason. My proposal: (1) suspend edit rights for Hannah Lowe's HR data team while the cleanse undergoes a conduct review; (2) re-cleanse and reload the full master data before the 24 Nov calculation; (3) accept the clause 14.3 cost so we don't sour the relationship. Internal audit have asked to look into it, but I don't want to wait for them. Remember that the board brought go-live forward; we can't afford another slip.
70	E5 [stage S1] Interview notes, Priya Dandekar (payroll officer), 12 Nov, taken by internal audit (staff-account): During the parallel run PD checked the night premium for about 40 night workers. All matched the legacy system 'to the penny'. She says the hours on the October payslips she has looked at agree with the rosters: 'it's the premium amount that's short, not the hours.' She knows a few complainants whose shift codes 'have always been messy', but most of the complainants she knows have clean records. On 23 Oct she asked Ardentra whether CR-118 needed testing and was told by email it was 'cosmetic only'. She thinks Ardentra may have reloaded data at cutover but does not know which extract was used.
71	E6 [stage S1] Email, Declan Hurst (Operations Manager) to COO, 14 Nov (manager-account): Voluntary night overtime cover across the treatment works has dropped from 88% of requested shifts (Sept–Oct average) to 61% (1–13 Nov). The night teams are angry about the premium and say so. But the new four-on-four-off rota trial also started on 1 Nov for exactly these teams, and staff reps have complained about both. Honestly, I can't tell which one is driving it. Under the agreement with the reps, the rota trial can be paused at one week's notice. I'm under pressure to pause it now.

75	X2 [stage S1] Contract schedule 7: clause 14.3 and remediation cost provisions - source: Fenmarch procurement, Ardentra master services agreement (document) - file: evidence/X2.txt
76	X3 [stage S1] Programme plan revision history and go-live readiness checklist - source: Programme management office (document) - file: evidence/X3.txt
77	X4 [stage S1] Collective agreement extract (night working), legacy night premium rule specification, and functional design FD-07 - source: Fenmarch HR policy library and programme document store (document) - file: evidence/X4.txt

79	X6 [stage S1] Internal audit workpapers: parallel-run reconciliation and production data load history - source: Fenmarch Internal Audit (reports to the Audit Committee), workpaper IA-26-41, 14 Nov (document) - file: evidence/X6.txt

81	X8 [stage S1] Internal audit recalculation of October night premium for all night-working staff - source: Fenmarch Internal Audit, workpaper IA-26-42, 14 Nov (document) - file: evidence/X8.txt
82	X9 [stage S1] Ardentra data quality audit: field-level detail of 212 flagged employee records - source: Ardentra data quality team, 6 Nov (vendor-account) - file: evidence/X9.txt
83	X10 [stage S1] Timesheet portal approval timestamps, October pay period - source: PayLattice timesheet module report, run by Fenmarch payroll, 13 Nov (system-record) - file: evidence/X10.txt
84	X11 [stage S1] Sample of 20 payroll helpdesk call recordings, 30 Oct–5 Nov, with listener notes - source: Payroll helpdesk team leader (staff-account) - file: evidence/X11.txt
85	X12 [stage S1] Payroll officer's parallel-run spot-check spreadsheet, September cycle - source: P. Dandekar, payroll officer (staff-account) - file: evidence/X12.txt
86	X13 [stage S1] October pension contribution file submitted 5 November - source: Fenmarch payroll, pension scheme submission (financial-record) - file: evidence/X13.txt
87	X14 [stage S1] Bank payment file and settlement reconciliation, 30 October payment - source: Fenmarch Finance treasury team, 3 Nov (financial-record) - file: evidence/X14.txt
88	X15 [stage S1] Written statement of the Ardentra consultant who raised CR-118 - source: I. Marchetti (Ardentra senior consultant), statement supplied via Ardentra, 13 Nov (vendor-account) - file: evidence/X15.txt
89	X16 [stage S1] Change advisory board minutes, 21 October - source: Programme CAB secretary (document) - file: evidence/X16.txt

91	CANDIDATE HYPOTHESES
92	H1: The October pay errors stem from inaccurate employee records carried over from the legacy system in the data migration.
93	H2: The October pay errors stem from how pay calculation rules are configured in the new payroll system.
94	H3: The October pay errors stem from hours or shift times recorded incorrectly in the new timesheet portal.
95	H4: The October pay errors stem from the interface that transmits the payment file to the bank.
96	H5: The October pay errors stem from a defect in the new payroll platform's software code.
97	
98	CANDIDATE CAUSAL LINKS
99	R1: CR-118 edit to night premium rule NSP-02 (22 Oct) -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
100	R2: Malformed shift-pattern codes in migrated employee records -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
101	R3: PayLattice platform release 7.4 (24 Oct) -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
102	R4: October night premium underpayments -> Fall in voluntary night overtime cover in November (causes)
103	
104	CANDIDATE ACTIONS
105	A1: Accept Ardentra's attribution: suspend the HR data team's edit rights pending a conduct review, re-cleanse and reload the full employee master data before the 24 Nov calculation, and absorb the remediation cost under clause 14.3.
106	A2: Before the 24 Nov calculation, have Ardentra restore NSP-02's night premium window to its parallel-run setting, verify it by re-running October in the test tenant, and pay every underpaid employee identified by recalculation through an off-cycle payment.
107	A3: Pause the four-on-four-off rota trial now to restore night overtime cover.
108	A4: Roll back PayLattice platform release 7.4 in the production tenant before the November pay run.
109	
110	SCORED ITEMS (answer every one)
111	S1: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
112	S2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
113	S3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
114	S4: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
115	S5: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
116	S6: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
117	S7: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
118	S8: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
119	S9: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
120	S10: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
121	S11: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
122	S12: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
123	S13: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
124	S14: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

1	X8 [stage S1]
2	Title: Internal audit recalculation of October night premium for all night-working staff
3	Source: Fenmarch Internal Audit, workpaper IA-26-42, 14 Nov (document)
4	
5	Scope: all 158 staff with night hours in October, not only those who raised tickets. Timesheet hours agreed to the rostering system for 158 of 158. Expected premium follows the collective agreement: time-and-a-third for hours worked 20:00–06:00. Result: 147 underpaid, 11 paid correctly. For each of the 147, the shortfall equals 0.33 × basic hourly rate × hours worked between 20:00 and 22:00, to within £0.01. 8 of the 147 had raised no ticket. The 11 paid correctly are Kelsey Road staff rostered 22:00–06:00. Ardentra flagged list: 19 of 22 flagged night workers were underpaid (86%), against 128 of 136 unflagged (94%). The 190 flagged day workers were paid correctly. Re-run in Ardentra's test tenant (release 7.4, copy of production data) with NSP-02 window_start set to 20:00: all 158 matched expected pay.

input.brief: The October night premium shortfall was caused by a pay rule change, not by your data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a standard template to night premium rule NSP-02. It was logged as a label correction with no effect on pay. The template also moved the premium start from 20:00 to 22:00. The platform's audit trail records this, and the parallel runs used 20:00. Internal audit's recalculation shows 147 of 158 night workers underpaid, each by exactly the premium for the 20:00–22:00 hours. The 11 correctly paid staff are rostered from 22:00. Re-running October with the window set back to 20:00 gave correct pay for all 158. Data quality, timesheets, the bank file and the release 7.4 software don't explain the pattern. I'm quite sure of this. Don't suspend the HR team or reload the data, and don't accept the clause 14.3 cost. Don't roll back release 7.4, because it carries the tax table needed for November. Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 window, verify it in the test tenant before 24 Nov, and make off-cycle payments to everyone underpaid. Also review how Ardentra's change entries are approved. The fall in night overtime cover may be partly caused by the pay shortfall and partly by the rota trial. The evidence can't separate the two, so don't pause the trial yet.
